Safety & recovery

Resolve an unknown outcome

Resolve the outcome of the original operation without applying the same edit again.

  • Before you begin
  • Follow the steps
  • Check the result
  • If something goes wrong
  • Continue with a related guide

Before you begin

  • The original operation reference, its account/device scope and the affected document/artifact identity.
  • Access to the original journal and eligible read-only inspection path; preserve current evidence.

Follow the steps

  1. Pause dependent changes

    Stop further writes, connector update/removal and replacement attempts that depend on the uncertain document result. Keep the document and journals.

    Checkpoint: No new affected write obscures whether the original edit happened.

  2. Find the original reference

    Open the structured activity/recovery entry for the uncertain operation. Keep its exact ID and selected document, rather than using a fresh request to test the outcome.

    Checkpoint: The status/reconciliation request refers to that same original operation.

  3. Inspect without applying

    Use the available Reconcile/read-status action. It reads journal, affected identities/revisions and artifact receipts; it must not open a new mutation transaction or repeat the command.

    Checkpoint: The result carries evidence for not dispatched, succeeded, failed with no effect, partial effect or still unknown.

  4. Follow the classified result

    For succeeded, inspect/import the existing verified receipt. For proven not-dispatched/no-effect, review a new intent only after fresh context. For partial effect, inspect the actual remaining state before planning recovery.

    Checkpoint: The next action is based on the original effect classification, not on a timeout or a generic success banner.

  5. Keep unresolved outcomes held

    If manual edits or missing evidence prevent proof, leave reconciliation required. Preserve safe references and ask Support. Only a matching outcome for this operation can resolve its hold.

    Checkpoint: A delayed receipt from another operation cannot clear the current unknown.

  6. Check usage separately

    Read the original provider reservation/receipt under its frozen wallet. Native cancellation, no-effect or reconciliation completion does not independently settle model usage.

    Checkpoint: Native outcome and financial outcome each have their own known or pending record.

Check the result

  • The exact original operation has a supported outcome with evidence, or stays explicitly unknown.
  • No duplicate edit, automatic undo, blind refund or unrelated receipt is used to manufacture completion.

If something goes wrong

  • The original reference is missing or the status action is unavailable.

    Keep the hold. Record build, host/document label, time and redacted activity references for Support. Do not invent a replacement status request or send the edit again.

    Resume from: Original operation recovered by an authorized inspection path.

  • The host was manually edited after the uncertain operation.

    Preserve that fact and current document. Read-only comparison may be insufficient; keep unknown instead of guessing from visible geometry.

    Resume from: Enough original evidence for a supported classification.

  • You canceled or the watchdog expired.

    Read the original state. Cancellation after dispatch is cooperative; watchdog expiry neither kills the host nor proves rollback.

    Resume from: Proven original effect, not elapsed time.

Availability and verification

Reconciliation needs the original installed native journal and read-only host evidence. If the build cannot look up that operation, keep the hold and contact Support.

  • Actual host reconciliation, original-operation lookup and provider settlement remain unqualified by this task.
  • A missing implementation path is an unavailable state, not permission to create a fake terminal result.
